# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain s158 (`%13`, 2026-09-09 11:09 → 11:40 AEST — the systemTest half of the first two-seat parallel run) | **BOTH items to READY FOR QA, PR #916 on origin with 13/13 preflight — and a PRECONDITION Wednesday set turned out to change the design rather than merely confirm it.** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **Verified independently by Wednesday:** `584b12ba1eed99583ec60141c41dce524c926dfe` at `refs/heads/kamilkreiser/ks-993-systemtest-typecheck-entrypoint` via `ls-remote`, with a positive control (develop present) and a negative control (bogus ref, 0 lines). **THE PRECONDITION PAID, and this is the row's headline:** Wednesday made *"survey what would pick that file up BEFORE you create it"* a requirement rather than a caveat. The survey found the audit sweeps are **lockfile-driven** (`lock-discovery.mjs` reads `git ls-files '*package-lock.json'`) — **so declaring `typescript` as a devDependency would have created `systemTest/package-lock.json` and carried its transitive advisories into the audit gate that is currently THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON EVERY PUSH IN THIS REPO.** The package therefore declares **no dependencies at all** and borrows the suites' pinned `typescript ^6.0.3`. **The seat's own line: *"'it is my file' would indeed not have answered that."*** It also named the two consumers that DO match (`preflight` leg 10, 48 → 49 with both enumerations agreeing; two retired Actions workflows matching `**/package.json`) and four that cannot reach it. **Q3 answered by THREE INDEPENDENT WITNESSES rather than a judgement:** `env_flags.ts:61`, the pre-existing test fixtures, and `secrets.example.yml` all read `secrets.secrets[environment]`, so `SecretsConfig` was right and the loop was wrong — *"no reading survived that contradicted them, so this was not a coin toss and is not a QUESTION."* **KS-1026 filed AND fixed** carrying all three required elements — the runtime proof both arms, the consequence stated plainly (*the k6 suite has been running on `secrets.yml` credentials the entire time it was believed to be running on provisioned actors*), and the vacuous ordering guard recorded as an instance rather than filed as a defect, with **the honest note that it needed no change and the fix makes it meaningful for the first time.** **Class census closed with a control:** 18 tracked `.sh`, 5 contain `rm -rf` (the non-zero control), only those 2 pair it with a `cp -R` snapshot. **#904 untouched as ruled; KS-1027 is ONE ticket per Kam's aggregation rule.** ⚠ **And it reported its preflight refusal as a FINDING rather than as something it got past:** leg 1 failed on a fresh worktree with no `node_modules`, and **the gate diagnosed its own false-positive mode** — *"DEPS MISSING … This is NOT spec drift"* — which is what stopped the honest reading being *"my typecheck change broke the spec"*. `npm ci`, 18s, 13/13, no `--no-verify`. |
| QA agent (fleet, Secuura KS-754 / PR #914 @ `311dc1ae4` — TIER 1 round 1, 2026-09-09 11:09 → 11:25) | **GO WITH FINDINGS on the PR the entire repo was blocked behind — and it DROVE the question rather than reasoning about it, on a live Postgres it stood up and removed.** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **Q1 was the blocker-shaped question and it answered it with three driven cells and two independent controls:** a throw at step 12 skips the USER_ERASED fan-out **after** the crypto-shred. `S3` head+injection → `success=false DEK=1 USER_ERASED=0`; **`CTL-A` head, injection OFF** isolates the injection as cause; **`CTL-B` base + the SAME injection** holds DB and injection fixed and varies **only the code**, isolating the

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.
